decisions.reason: The complete declared files contain only the two value models, panel and private state/identity/text/action/color/style helpers. No unrelated declarations or global side effects appear. This does not assess unlisted upstream files.

The declared public Swift Equatable models and public View initializer match the exact fields and callback signatures; Swift uses APIs available in iOS 14. Kotlin data classes, package and @Composable function match the approved signatures. Source API observation only.
Both implementations take caller values directly and iterate options in caller order without imposing a narrower domain. Neither file introduces audio or network operations.
All eleven fixed listening identifiers and the listening.option.<id> construction are declared at their intended views/controls. This source observation does not prove native query reachability.

Option handlers assign the single selected ID, clear error, and guard started/unavailable input; reselecting preserves the ID. Disabled predicates include unavailable and started states. Source control-flow observation only.

Both primary handlers resolve an available selected option, distinguish the three exact fixed validation strings, and return without callback on unmet conditions. Source control-flow observation only.

Cancel is not disabled by local state; its handler resets all four local fields and calls the current onCancel with input.sessionID exactly once on each activation. Source control-flow observation only.

Option selection and acknowledgement setters clear error. Acknowledgement setters allow false during editing and preserve selection; started guards/disabled predicates prevent editing afterward. Source control-flow observation only.

Swift keys the stateful child by a Hashable identity whose equality compares complete Equatable input and whose hash incorporates every ordered option field. Kotlin remember(input) creates new local state for unequal full input. Equal input retains the state and the replacement path emits no callback. Source state ownership only; no unexecuted runtime replacement result is claimed.

Unknown: the declared evidence contains only the production component files; neither supplied bridge is in this row's declared file scope. Product-local state is visible, but the universal claim about bridge behavior cannot be established here.

The explicit opaque RGB/ARGB literals match all eleven approved roles, and the view/helper call sites route heading/body/detail/error/option/primary/Cancel roles as specified. No source shadows, gradients or translucency are added. This is source composition only, not computed pixel color.

The source declares the single full-width leading column, 20 padding, 12 block/option gaps and circular corners, 4 option text gap, 16 horizontal and 12 vertical content padding, and 1 option border. Primary/action text sits inside the padding with no border/icons/decorations in the side bands. This does not infer computed spacing from AX.

Swift ScaledMetric supplies 24/16/14 system fonts with explicit regular/semibold roles; Kotlin uses scaled sp 24/16/14, Default system family and Normal/SemiBold role arguments. Source font declarations only; no runtime font measurement is claimed.

Unknown: keeping review methods separate is an integration/evaluation obligation. These declared production component files contain no native evidence evaluator or review procedure to establish that proposition.

Unknown: checkpoint fixation, successful observer dispatch qualification and callback-interval adjudication belong to the observer/evaluator. Those sources are outside this row's declared component-only evidence scope.

Only the valid primary branch and Cancel handler call the supplied closures, with current input IDs; selection/toggle/error/reset/Choose again/recomposition and input identity paths contain no callback invocation. Closures are current view/composable parameters, not retained in remembered state. Source control-flow only.

Text helper applies leading/Start multiline and frame alignment; option columns use leading/Start; action labels reuse that text helper. Swift Toggle is standard trailing-switch style, Kotlin row places weighted label before Switch. This is modifier/layout intent in source, not a computed geometry assertion.

The validated primary handler directly assigns started=true and clears error before one onStart(input.sessionID, selectedOption.id); there is no timer, task or dispatch. Source handler ordering only; pixel rendering timing is not established.

The action label has horizontal 16 and vertical 12 padding, circular rounded radius 12 fill/contentShape in Swift, and a full-width Material Button with circular RoundedCornerShape(12.dp), matching content padding and no border/decorations in Kotlin. The primary text remains in the inner label content area. Source composition only, not physical hit-region measurement.
